quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A person is legally intoxicated if their blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is at least ______.
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to drive a motorcycle or car while intoxicated.

questions.question: Before riding your motorcycle, you should check everything except:
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. You do not need to check the paint.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be worn because they:

options.text: Keep your hands from getting too hot
Give you a better grip on the handlebars
Make it easier to control the motorcycle
Are only necessary on cold days

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars
questions.explanation: Wear leather gloves or gloves made of another durable material. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake
Use both brakes at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: Apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes involve riders who have owned their motorcycle for less than six months. Most crashes occur during the day at low speeds.

questions.question: Which option provides the best face protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: A motorcycle that fits you properly allows you to:

options.text: Touch the ground with your feet while sitting
Have the seat even with your waist
Have the seat 10 inches above your waist
Have the seat 10 inches below your waist

questions.correctAnswerText: Touch the ground with your feet while sitting
questions.explanation: Your feet should be able to touch the ground while you are seated on a properly-fitted motorcycle. Keep your feet on the footrests while riding.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in the front and rear
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in the front and rear
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: Before carrying a passenger in traffic for the first time, you should:

options.text: Flash your lights so others see you
Practice on the shoulder of a road

questions.explanation: Practice riding on a quiet road before you carry a passenger or heavy load in traffic. This helps you get used to how your motorcycle handles with extra weight.

questions.question: When a motorcycle operator extends their left arm straight out to the left, it means they:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle operators use hand signals instead of turn signals. A left arm extended straight out means the operator plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slow down by releasing the throttle. Brake gently on the good tire if you know which one it is. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down. Then squeeze the clutch and stop.

questions.question: What kind of penalties does Oregon have for drinking and riding?

options.text: Up to a judge to decide.

questions.explanation: Oregon law has severe penalties for drinking and riding. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see better and be seen. It keeps you away from blind spots, wind blasts, and road hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and should give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, riders should pass one at a time. The second rider waits until the first rider is safely back in the original lane before passing. This pattern continues until all riders have passed safely.

questions.question: What usually causes a rider to move into another lane while turning?
questions.explanation: Entering a turn at too high a speed may cause you to drift into another lane or off the road.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is usually on the left handlebar of a motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars loosely to allow movement.
Hold the handlebars firmly to maintain control.
Use lots of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it doesn't cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly when riding over rough surfaces. This keeps you in control of your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should you adjust?

options.text: Operate at a slower speed than usual.
Maintain a shorter following distance than when riding alone.
Operate at a faster speed than usual.
Brake a little later than when riding alone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Operate at a slower speed than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. Your bike will need more time to speed up, slow down, and turn. Ride slower, start slowing earlier, increase your following distance, and look for bigger gaps when turning or merging.

questions.question: Where should you get information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The owner's manual is the best source of information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before operating your motorcycle for the first time.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handlebar. Know the location of all controls before riding.

questions.question: Why is riding directly next to another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have trouble reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing you both.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The driver may change lanes without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your way to escape if danger occurs.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect riders?

options.text: They make it hard to focus.

questions.explanation: Most medicines for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or nerves make you sleepy and can hurt your ability to ride safely. Before riding, check how any medicine affects you.

questions.question: What causes the front wheel and handlebars to wobble or shake?

options.text: Brakes that do not work right.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles come from improper loading, bad accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help prevent serious injury?
questions.explanation: To protect yourself from injury, wear a DOT-approved helmet, face or eye protection, a jacket and long pants made of strong material, high and sturdy boots or shoes that cover your ankles, and durable gloves.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that inform drivers of road rules, such as speed limits, are rectangular with white background and black lettering or symbols. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.
